teams.synopsis: Best team he's ever drafted — CeeDee, Jacobs, and Adams in the first three rounds, with only Pollard as a real weakness.
teams.blurb: Finally, the top-ranked team. Quin comes in at #1 on these preseason rankings with, in my opinion, his best team he's ever had. Quin made all the right picks — <mark class="hl-player">CeeDee</mark> in the 1st round, <mark class="hl-player">Jacobs</mark> in the 2nd round, <mark class="hl-player">Adams</mark> in the 3rd round, I could go on all day. With no <mark class="hl-player">Aiyuk</mark> in Pittsburgh, <mark class="hl-player">Pickens</mark> has an opportunity to be a legitimate top-15 wide receiver. Additionally, <mark class="hl-player">Engram</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Love</mark> aren't top players at their positions but can have great seasons that keep them in the top 5. The one weakness everyone will point to is <mark class="hl-player">Tony Pollard</mark> at RB2, but I believe that with some trading, or potentially just some luck, Quin can find himself a viable RB2 to contribute to this top roster.

teams.synopsis: Mr. Consistent — two elite PPR RBs and a stacked roster, with only the flex spots left unproven.
teams.blurb: Mr. Consistent. Andrew comes in at 2nd, and I don't think there's any argument for him being out of the top 3, at least. He was able to pick up two elite PPR running backs who, yes, are getting older, but still can produce at an elite level. At the 4/5 turn, Andrew got an elite quarterback and an elite tight end to finish setting the foundation of his stacked roster. Now, he may have made a questionable pick with <mark class="hl-player">Deebo</mark> over <mark class="hl-player">Adams</mark>, and his WR2 and flex are somewhat unproven young players, but if those guys hit — and maybe even <mark class="hl-player">Chase Brown</mark> becomes something off his bench — then Andrew will continue to solidify himself as a top team and a top manager in the league.

teams.synopsis: Two top-5-upside RBs and a strong WR corps — just missing that one iconic star every champion seems to have.
teams.blurb: The runner-up from 2022 is trying to make his way back to the top. Ryan opened his 2024 draft with back-to-back running backs, <mark class="hl-player">Isiah Pacheco</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Travis Etienne</mark>. Both players have top-5 upside at the position, and when you combine that with a top tight end and three wide receivers with top-25 capability weekly, you get a top-5 team in the league. Ryan's weakest spot is his quarterback, but when <mark class="hl-player">Purdy</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Goff</mark> finish as top-15 quarterbacks, everyone will be envying Quad's Squad. I don't have this team any higher than 3rd, simply because it lacks that iconic star every championship team seems to have.

teams.synopsis: A top-10 WR, RB, and QB make up for the Diggs pick — Goedert at TE is the one soft spot.
teams.blurb: As we enter the top 4, I'll just say that most of the teams at the top are interchangeable, and this is just the order I decided on. As mentioned, I'm not the biggest fan of Houston wide receivers because of the uncertainty of target share across all of them this season; however, Aidan's team has a top-10 wide receiver, running back, and quarterback to make up for the <mark class="hl-player">Stefon Diggs</mark> pick. I believe <mark class="hl-player">Godwin</mark> will be better than Evans this season and establish himself as a top-25 wide receiver in fantasy. <mark class="hl-player">Mixon</mark> has to solidify himself in a new offense, but no matter what, having the starting running back for a top-5 offense will be rewarding. Finally, the biggest weakness on this team is <mark class="hl-player">Goedert</mark> at tight end, but if the rest of the team plays to its potential, this team will be a true top team.

teams.synopsis: A great start with Amon-Ra, Puka, and Achane — the only real worry is age at RB2 with Aaron Jones.
teams.blurb: As I said on the podcast, I think Baylen had a great start to his draft with <mark class="hl-player">Amon-Ra</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Puka</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Achane</mark>, and although I'm not as high on <mark class="hl-player">Richardson</mark> as consensus is, I still think he'll be a top-5-to-7 quarterback this season. Baylen has <mark class="hl-player">Pitts</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">McConkey</mark> as his tight end and flex, respectively, both set to explode this season. My least favorite player on this roster is <mark class="hl-player">Aaron Jones</mark>, due to his age, new situation, and injury history — it's not common for older running backs to change teams and produce, but it's definitely possible. This all leads me to placing Baylen at the 5th spot.

teams.synopsis: Lamar gives this team a huge edge at QB, but the flex and thin bench remain real question marks.
teams.blurb: There are rumors he was laying up during the draft — maybe he wasn't all there — but still, Brandon found a way to draft a great team. Having an elite quarterback is a hot commodity in a 14-man league, as we saw with the QB frenzy on Sunday night, so Brandon securing <mark class="hl-player">Lamar</mark> was a great way to separate himself from half the league. A wide receiver tandem of <mark class="hl-player">Jefferson</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">DK</mark> will feed families, because both have top-15, if not top-10, upside this season. An average running back and tight end dynamic kept this team in the top half of the rankings, while the flex of <mark class="hl-player">Watson</mark> tried to bring it down. I'm not the biggest fan of Watson, and with little bench depth, it'll be intriguing to see if Brandon makes a trade to acquire a more reliable flex.

teams.synopsis: An old-guys running back trio and a sneaky WR duo — could be the league's best roster, or could bust entirely.
teams.blurb: The front man for the league's new podcast, Max himself has a solid team that shouldn't be forgotten about when talking about the top teams in the league. A running back trio of <mark class="hl-player">Barkley</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Henry</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Mostert</mark> may seem too old to be league-winning, but some would argue age is just a number. Max was able to get <mark class="hl-player">Kincaid</mark> in the 5th, a steal in my opinion. The wide receiver duo of <mark class="hl-player">Nabers</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Keenan Allen</mark> is also sneaky. I placed this team right in the middle of the rankings, because if his old guys don't regress and his young guys break out, this will be the best roster in the league — but that's a big if, and it's probably just as likely for this team to bust.

teams.synopsis: The best RB duo in the league on paper — but the WR trio's range runs from 75 combined to 25.
teams.blurb: Getting ready to make another deep playoff run, Charlie finds himself in the middle of the pack for the first rankings of the season. In my opinion, he was able to draft the best running back duo in the league with <mark class="hl-player">Taylor</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Kyren</mark>, so that alone gives him a chance to put up big points any given week. However, Charlie was unable to draft <mark class="hl-player">Blake Corum</mark>, so Kyren's injury risk will be crucial to his success. Having an elite tight end will always be helpful as well. The issues with this team lie in the wide receivers, where <mark class="hl-player">Higgins</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Ridley</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Kirk</mark> can have wildly varying production — either 75 combined or 25 combined. Additionally, an eye should be kept on <mark class="hl-player">Daniels</mark> as he progresses as a rookie quarterback.

teams.synopsis: An incredible WR trio and the Hurts + Smith stack, but a shaky RB room caps the ceiling early.
teams.blurb: The reigning champ finds himself at 9th in the rankings to begin the 2024 season. The first thing that stands out when you look at this team is the running back duo of <mark class="hl-player">Javonte Williams</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Jaylen Warren</mark>, and with the only notable running backs on the bench being <mark class="hl-player">Spears</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Allgeier</mark>, a trade for a top running back is inevitable. Now, there are positives to Carmine's team — the incredible WR trio of <mark class="hl-player">Wilson</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Olave</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Smith</mark>, and the <mark class="hl-player">Hurts</mark> + Smith stack that will help Carmine get back to the top of the rankings. However, I still believe the lack of viable running backs on this team will cap its ceiling to begin the year.

teams.synopsis: An unproven QB and weak TE keep this low, but the Waddle pickup gave Evans room to underperform.
teams.blurb: Dude — dude, yeah, Anthony, you're 10th to begin the season. Back in a familiar place, Anthony is ranked low to start the year because of a few factors: an unproven quarterback, a very weak tight end, and a couple of old heads at RB2 and WR2. Personally, I think <mark class="hl-player">Evans</mark> will regress a little after having his best fantasy season since 2016 last year, so the 2nd-round pick may have been a reach. However, picking up <mark class="hl-player">Waddle</mark> in the 3rd allowed Evans a little freedom to underperform. <mark class="hl-player">Breece</mark> is my pick for RB1 this season, but having <mark class="hl-player">Conner</mark> as his RB2 is tricky, given Conner has missed 4+ games in four of the last five seasons. Still, solid bench depth will help Anthony through the missed time and keep him on track to get back into the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: The Hero RB strategy paid off with Bijan, but the WR room is a real gamble — lowest floor, highest ceiling in the league.
teams.blurb: There's a lot to like about Deniz's team — he went with my favorite draft strategy (Hero RB) and took <mark class="hl-player">Bijan</mark> in the first round, then filled out his wide receivers. However, I don't love the wide receivers he filled it out with; as I said on the podcast, I was avoiding the Texans and Bears wide receivers due to uncertainty over who commands the targets, and it just happens that Deniz's WR1 and WR2 are <mark class="hl-player">Nico</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">DJ</mark>. Still, he has the <mark class="hl-player">Stroud</mark> + Nico stack and isn't totally lost at RB2 and tight end. I'd argue this team has the lowest floor and one of the highest ceilings in the league, and only time will tell us which one it is.

teams.synopsis: The Panthers' offense is the whole question mark here — tremendous upside, none of it proven yet.
teams.blurb: Placing myself at 12th was an easy choice — simply put, it came down to the question marks surrounding the Panthers' offense this season. I believe it'll provide a couple of fantasy gems, but we've yet to see that. Additionally, I was the last person to take a quarterback in the draft, so a lot of faith is riding on <mark class="hl-player">Trevor Lawrence</mark> or <mark class="hl-player">Matt Stafford</mark> providing good fantasy production on a weekly basis. This team has tremendous upside, but until we see that, I believe this ranking is truly fair.

teams.synopsis: Two solid RBs, an elite QB and WR1 — but the flex and TE need to break out for this to be elite.
teams.blurb: Rankings will change a lot and players will prove me wrong, as they always have, but the runner-up from 2023 looks like he won't get back to the championship for the 2nd year in a row. Cole's 2024 squad consists of 2 solid running backs that will most likely finish in the RB10-RB25 range, an elite quarterback who should get back into the top 5 at the position this season, and an elite WR who could finish at the top of the position, plus a solid WR2 in <mark class="hl-player">Pittman</mark>. However, he's ranked 13th to start the season because of his flex and tight end — he'll need his young players to break out to have an elite team this time around.

teams.synopsis: Poor RBs and shaky TE play sink him last, but a top-15 WR trio could change that fast.
teams.blurb: Ben comes into this season with a lot to prove, since he came in 13th last season and hasn't made the playoffs since 2021. Poor running backs and questionable tight ends make it easy to place Ben low on the first week's rankings, but if <mark class="hl-player">Tyreek</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">London</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Aiyuk</mark> can all put up top-15 WR numbers, then this team will be something. <mark class="hl-player">Joe Burrow</mark> will also be an intriguing player to watch, since his 2023 season was underwhelming for fantasy managers. I expect this ranking to change as early as Week 2, as the season kicks off on Thursday.
